title: The danger of not recognising the Grace of God Part 2
scripture_text: “Meanwhile, the older son was in the field. When he came near the house, he heard music and dancing So he called one of the servants and asked him what was going on.‘Your brother has come,’ he replied, ‘and your father has killed the fattened calf because he has him back safe and sound.’ “The older brother became angry and refused to go in. So his father went out and pleaded with him. But he answered his father, ‘Look! All these years I’ve been slaving for you and never disobeyed your orders. Yet you never gave me even a young goat so I could celebrate with my friends. But when this son of yours who has squandered your property with prostitutes comes home, you kill the fattened calf for him!’ ‘My son,’ the father said, ‘you are always with me, and everything I have is yours. But we had to celebrate and be glad, because this brother of yours was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found.’’
devotional:
The thinking of the eldest son.

His thinking was perhaps conditioned by his circumstances. The way this elder brother thought would have developed over many years.

Now in the first part of the Parable we have very little mention of the eldest son. All we know about him that he had a father and a younger brother.

Now, the people listening to Jesus would have picked up on the lack of activity of the elder son in the first part of the parable, for in that culture it was the responsibility of an elder son to mediate between his younger brother and his father. He had a cultural obligation to try a broker a peace between his brother and his father. He was the best placed person who had an opportunity to try and find a solution to the crisis the family was now experiencing.

This elder brother however was pragmatic when it came to his responsibilities. It suited him better to stand back and say nothing. He was going to gain sooner if his father carried out the request of his younger brother before his fathers death.

His silence therefore indicated, that his own personal gain was more important than the well-being of his father and brother and their relationship.

Sometimes we need to step up and take responsibility for situations, it is often too easy for us to step back and say ‘it’s not my issue, I’m not getting involved!’

Sometimes people remain silent because they feel insecure, or they don’t like confrontation. However, this was not the case with the elder son, as we shall see he had no problem with confronting others. His silence was really an expression of selfishness. The inactivity of the elder brother turned him into someone who could not understand or display grace. Remaining silent when he knew he should have spoken, began the process of him developing into a person who could not or would not understand grace.

He was an angry man.

Jesus wants us to know what was going on in the heart of this older brother. He was angry! Jesus does not tell us who he is angry with or why. He may have been angry because of the actions of his father, in throwing such a lavish party for his younger brother. (In giving the party the father had to use the elder brothers’ resources which of course he wouldn’t have been happy about.)

On a surface level we could probably sympathise with the elder brother. He had stayed at home and worked hard in order to protect the part inheritance he had received. Now here was his father using his inheritance to splash out on a big party for his irresponsible brother who had just returned. However, if we go a bit deeper and look beyond the surface, we will realise that for the elder brother, his possessions was all he had. He was the kind of person who measured his value and success by the things he possessed. His distance from his father produced in him a materialistic mindset ‘what I possess is more important that my relationships, and if you touch my stuff I will get angry.’

Anger is not always wrong, but it was in this case as it was an expression of blatant selfishness. His anger prevented him from understanding, receiving or showing grace.

He had no respect for his Father. Listen to how he talks to his father. His first word is ‘Look,’ in using this word he refused to give his father the respect that he was due. You can almost feel his anger ‘Look!’

He thought of himself as a slave not a son! His father had pleaded with him to come in but he would not listen. So after he is rude to his father he begins to talk about himself. ‘All these years I have been slaving for you and never disobeyed your orders.’ What a tragic statement! We need to understand that our ability to understand, enjoy and live in the reality of grace, depends on us choosing to live as sons and daughters of God.
prayer: Father thank you that your desire for us is that we live with the realisation that we are your children.
